spoken_transcript: Most traders open a footprint chart and get lost in the numbers, but there's one thing I look for every day, stacked and balances. An imbalance is where buyers hit the ass three times harder than sellers hit the bit more. One imbalance, that's noise, but three or more stacks together, that's aggressive buyers lifting every level, they're not waiting. They need to get filled. Now here's the key. When price comes back to that zone, those same buyers defend it. If it holds, that's your long, but if it breaks, those buyers are trapped, and they become fuel for the move down. Don't trade the numbers to trade who's stuck.

I never thought I’d be a trader. Not even when I first got into it.

I graduated high school with a 2.0, and that was me trying just enough to keep playing sports. Football was supposed to be my thing. When that didn’t work out in college, I didn’t know what to do with myself.

So I gave school a real shot. Lasted maybe two months. I’d sit in class thinking, “what am I doing here?” So I left.

That’s when my mom got on me every single day. Get a job, what are you doing with your life. I get it now, but at the time it was hard. So I worked. Lowe’s, Amazon, warehouses, whatever. I bounced around so much I lost count.

I was really depressed. I’d stand in that warehouse staring at the clock thinking, is this just my life now?

Somewhere in there, I started trading on my phone during lunch breaks. Just something to look at that wasn’t that clock. I went all in on ICT and still couldn’t make it work. Three years of losing. Blowing accounts.

But I didn’t stop. I couldn’t go back to that clock.

I got a sales job, started making real money, and every bit of it went into trading. Then I found order flow and it was like, oh. This is what I was missing. Things started working. I quit sales and put everything into this.

Now I just trade. I couldn’t care less about a mansion or a Lambo. I just wanted to do what I wanted, on my own time. Now I live in a nice place, have a nice car, and can do whatever I want, whenever I want.

The 2.0 kid who couldn’t sit through a class now studies charts all day. Guess I just needed something I actually cared about.

Almost nobody knows. Not my family. Not even my mom. She probably still thinks I’m figuring it out. Maybe one day I’ll sit her down and show her all of it. The losses, the blown accounts, the nights at this desk. I think she’d be proud.

If you’re stuck at a job you hate, staring at the clock like I was, I’m not telling you to go trade. I’m telling you it’s okay to not have it figured out yet.

Just don’t stop looking for your thing. 👍

spoken_transcript: That right there is called an iceberg. So price kept hitting into a level over and over again and it just could not break it. That's because someone with a big size limit order is sitting there that you could not see. An iceberg is called an iceberg because it's a huge order but it's only showing you a small piece of it on the order book. So on the order book you might only see 10 contracts at that level but as soon as those 10 get filled it will quietly reload it. Don't keep throwing orders into it thinking that it will break but it just absorbs them all. This is something that you can see with order flow that you can't see with normal canle sick charts.
